raw_response:
I have been farming this piece of land in Quzhou for 56 years. I am 70 now, and my wife and I manage our 4.1 mu together. My bones ache some mornings, but I still know every inch of this soil. I grow peanut because it suits our land and the market price has been steady. I plant in spring when the soil warms up — around the 19th of April — and harvest before the autumn rains, around early September.

This year, like last year, I will prepare the field with rotary tillage. Peanut needs a loose, fine seedbed so the pods can set properly underground. I will sow about 40 jin of improved seed per mu — I save half from my own crop and buy half new to keep the vigor up. The variety I use is an improved local type, similar to Haihua, which gives me reliable pods.

For fertilizer, I do not pour on too much nitrogen because peanut fixes its own from the air. I will spread about 25 kg per mu of general compound fertilizer — 15-15-15 — as basal dressing before sowing. When the plants flower, I will topdress once with a high-potash compound, about 10 kg per mu. In total, that gives me roughly 5 kg of nitrogen, 4 kg of phosphorus, and 8 kg of potassium per mu. That is enough for this soil; over-fertilizing makes the vines grow wild and reduces pod set.

I have a well, so I can irrigate when needed. But peanut does not like wet feet. I will irrigate twice: once around sowing if the spring is dry, and once during pod-filling in mid-summer. More than that and I risk root rot.

For crop protection, I spray three times. First, a herbicide after sowing to keep the weeds down — at my age, hoeing 4 mu is too hard on my back. Second, an insecticide once when I see aphids or webworms appear. Third, I apply a growth regulator during flowering to keep the vines from growing too tall and to help the pods develop underground. I do not usually need fungicide if the weather stays dry.

If the weather cooperates, I expect about 500 kg per mu. That has been my average these past few years, and I see no reason it should change if I stick to what I know.
